passage:
At nine at night, with a viva the next morning, Arnab's phone lit up with a message from a batchmate: "Is it true you're quitting engineering? Sorry to hear that." The only person he had told was Kalyani. His face went hot.

He wanted to type something cruel. He even opened the note where he kept what Kalyani had once confided about her failed paper, then closed it. Instead he wrote to her: "Can we talk after the viva? Just us."

The next day, on the library steps, he said, "I told only you. Now half the class knows. I'm angry, and I want to know what happened." Kalyani stared at her shoes. "I told one person. I didn't think it would go anywhere." Arnab nodded slowly. He didn't hug her. From now on he would share smaller things and watch what came back.

qa.q: What was Arnab feeling when he read the message, and what did he nearly do?
qa.a: Angry and exposed, with his face hot. He nearly used Kalyani's own confided secret against her but closed the note.

qa.q: What did Arnab do wisely in this situation?
qa.a: He waited until after the viva, asked to talk privately, told Kalyani how he felt and did not leak her secret in return.

qa.q: How might Kalyani have felt on the library steps?
qa.a: Ashamed or defensive. She stared at her shoes and said she didn't think it would go anywhere.

grounding: Arnab's secret spreads; he feels exposed and furious, confronts Kalyani privately and decides how much to trust her.

passage:
Chaitanya,
I'm writing because if I say this in person, I'll either shout or cry.
In August I told you, and only you, that I was repeating the semester because I kept freezing in exams. Yesterday three people in the lab asked me if I was "okay now". One of them said you'd mentioned it at Gautam's party.
I felt exposed, standing there in my lab coat with everyone looking. I was furious. For an hour I wanted to tell the whole class what you once told me about your brother. I'm not going to. I don't want to become that.
But you need to know: it hurt, and it changed things. I'm not ending our friendship in this letter, and I'm not pretending it's fine either. I'll be slower to share things with you now. If you want to talk, I'll listen, once, on Saturday in the reading room.
Nandini

qa.q: Where did someone say Chaitanya had mentioned the secret?
What did Nandini feel when three people in the lab asked about being "okay now"?
qa.a: Exposed and furious, with a brief urge to spread Chaitanya's own secret in return.

qa.q: What choices in the letter make it a wise response?
qa.a: Nandini confronts Chaitanya privately, refuses to leak Chaitanya's secret, and decides to share more carefully while offering one talk.

qa.q: How might Chaitanya feel reading the letter?
qa.a: Ashamed and worried about losing the friendship, but given a clear chance to talk on Saturday.

grounding: Shows a secret spread by a friend, feeling exposed and furious, and confronting privately instead of leaking their secrets back.

passage:
You know what Samir did, Rono? I told him in October that my parents are separating. Nobody else knew. Two weeks later, in the canteen, Pritam says, "Sorry about your folks." Just like that, in front of everyone.
I went hot all over. I wanted to post Samir's old messages about his crush in the group, right there. I had them. My thumb was on the screenshot.
I didn't. I walked out, and that evening I waited for Samir at the tea stall near the hostel gate. I said, "I trusted you with one thing. Why?" He went red and said he thought Pritam already knew. Maybe. Maybe not.
We're still friends, sort of. I sit with him in class. But I don't tell him anything that matters anymore, and I've told him that too.
Anyway, that's me, Arnab, learning to keep my own secrets closer.

qa.q: What did Arnab tell Samir in October?
What did Arnab feel when Pritam spoke about it in the canteen?
qa.a: Exposed and furious, "hot all over", with an urge to post Samir's messages in revenge.

qa.q: Which choice worked for Arnab, and why?
qa.a: Confronting Samir privately at the tea stall instead of leaking Samir's messages; Arnab kept dignity and could decide how much trust was left.

qa.q: How does Samir explain what happened?
qa.a: He goes red and says he thought Pritam already knew, which suggests he feels embarrassed and caught out.

grounding: Illustrates betrayal by gossip, the pull to retaliate with the friend's secrets, and instead confronting privately and trusting less.
